---
title: Events and webhooks
description: How an app learns what changed in an instance, by following the event stream or receiving webhooks, and how the owner hears what needs attention.
job: A builder learns how an app hears about changes, by the event log, the stream and webhooks.
kind: concept
---

An app that shows someone's data must know when another app changes it. Marfa records each change to an item or edge as an **event** in one ordered log. An event is a record of a change, not a `core.event` item, which holds a calendar event. An app pulls events from the **event stream** when it needs every change, including what it missed while away, or has Marfa push them as **webhooks** when a service just reacts.

<EventFlow />

## The event log

Each event has an **event type**, such as `item.created`, `edge.deleted` or `rows.changed`, and an item event carries the item as it stands after the change. Changes to items, tags, extensions, rows and edges add events. **Other writes add none,** such as a change to a type, a key or a setting. [Events](/catalog/events) in the Catalog lists them all.

Event IDs rise, so the last ID an app handled, its **cursor**, says exactly where it stopped. The log keeps events for 30 days by default. A credential sees only the events about what its [type map](/build/access#what-a-credential-reaches) lets it read.

## The event stream

The [event stream](/reference/api/event-stream/streamEvents) is a connection your app keeps open. The CLI follows it here while another app saves a note:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa events --type core.note
```

```text
-  stream_cursor  18
-  stream_live  18
19  item.created  01a1fc3e-8e45-7226-8bb7-63467062037f
```

</Terminal>

The stream replays every event after the cursor you send, marks the point you've caught up with `stream_live`, then sends each new event. Resume from your cursor and you get every later event **exactly once.** After a break longer than the log keeps events, the stream ends with `catchup_too_old` and the app reads its data again ([Keep a copy in sync](/build/keep-in-sync)). A [working copy](/build/working-copies) follows the stream for you.

## Webhooks

A webhook works the other way round: Marfa posts each new event to a URL you register, for the event types you choose, with a credential that holds `webhooks.manage`. **Each delivery is signed** in `X-Marfa-Signature`, so your service can check it came from your instance. A failure, a timeout or a `408` or `429` is tried again, eight times over a little more than five hours; any other `4xx` ends it at once.

**A webhook has no cursor and no replay:** it delivers only events written after you registered it, and they can arrive **out of order**, so a receiver keeps the highest event ID it applied for each item. A bulk write reaches webhooks only with `enable_fanout: true`, and a webhook posts only to a public address unless the owner sets `allow_private_addresses` ([Settings](/run/settings)). [Receive webhooks](/build/receive-webhooks) shows how to register one and check a delivery.

## When the owner needs to act

Marfa sends `attention.raised` when it finds something new that needs the owner's attention, such as a failed backup. **It reaches only a stream or webhook whose credential holds `instance.read`.** The event holds the entry's kind and a fixed description and **never its detail,** because a webhook posts outside the instance: `marfa attention` gives that. A webhook on it tells the owner.

The rules behind this page are in the [events](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/events.md) and [reach](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/reach.md) chapters of the contract.
